newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Bank of Korea sells dollars to support won-dealers.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Korea sells dollars to support won-dealers.

text.p: The Bank of Korea intervened in the interbank market in late Friday morning trade, selling dollars at 897.00 won to support the won, dealers said.
The won rose to 895.50 just after the central bank's intervention. It opened at 894.00 and touched 897.20, the lowest since the nation launched the market average system in March 1990.
Dealers said the central bank's release of February current account deficit figures pushed the dollar higher.
The bank said the deficit rose to $2.45 billion in February from $1.98 billion a year earlier.
